newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ciller remarks fail to satisfy Turkish investors.
newsitem.headline: Ciller remarks fail to satisfy Turkish investors.

text.p: Turkish financial markets shivered on Monday following renewed political turmoil, and despite a declaration by the government's conservative wing that the Islamist-led coalition would survive.
Share prices were fragile, the central bank stepped in to support the lira in currency markets, and bankers said political fears haunted the bond market.

Two ministers from the coalition's conservative wing quit at the weekend, citing fears that Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his Welfare Party were steering Turkey away from its Western vocation and trying to enforce Islam in public life.
Their True Path Party leader, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, on Monday reiterated her commitment to the government. "We will continue to work with stability," Ciller said.

Her remarks failed to fully restore optimism to the share market, whose index closed 1.71 percent down at 1,441 -- following a 4.3 percent fall last week amid growing uncertainty over the future of Erbakan's 10-month-old administration.

Brokers said Monday's trading was largely dominated by concerns following Saturday's National Security Council meeting, at which military members repeated a two-month-old demand for a crackdown against religious revival.
Earlier, markets opened to newspaper reports that some members of parliament from Ciller's party planned to force her to break up the coalition.

The Daily Hurriyet quoted former industry and trade minister Yalim Erez, who resigned on Saturday, as saying the government would collapse in a week, with the help of other dissidents from the junior coalition partner.
"We are likely to see a market stuck in a range of 1,420 and 1,500 unless political turmoil settles down," said Inci Bas, a broker at Deha Securities.

"The political tension has not yet been eliminated. The index may fall to 1,430 levels, but it may rise to over 1,440 level again on reaction buys, and get stuck in a narrow band between 1,440 and 1,450," said Serdar Surer from Ekinciler securities.
Okan Alpay from Interyatirim said the index was expected to find support at the 1,430 and 1,420 levels.
Some brokers said selective demand in some stocks might ease the bearish trend.
The lira closed lower at 135,200 to the dollar from Friday's close at 134,000. The central bank bought lira for dollars for the third consecutive day to support the local currency, traders said.
Money markets were stable, while bond rates fell two points in weak volume and nervous trading, after a five point decline last week.
"The negative political situation and high funding costs caused by liquidity shortage are major factors. Players prefer to keep cash rather than buy paper," said one banker.
